analysis:
Examined docs/threat-model.yaml BASE lines 1–897 and the supplied bounded patch against the canonical definition index and selected details. BASE establishes trusted coordinator hop-by-hop encryption (89–102), process-only X25519 custody and operator protections (336–442), inference cancellation/encryption/cache boundaries (444–515), privileged fan isolation (653–681), and independent App Attest authorization with final-handoff checks, bounded resumption and separate reward policy (683–797). Existing limitations are not PR regressions.
The patch adds an availability asset at HEAD 232–241 and begins a local add-on hold boundary at HEAD 811 onward; HEAD 43–45 describes signature checks, leases, machine-lock fallback and separate platform handling of busy fields. These additions introduce a local admission/availability interaction relevant to TB-003, TB-007, TB-002, T-010 and T-029. No supplied evidence establishes a weakened control or exploitable regression, so there is no supported finding.
Integration must reconcile the complete new boundary/threat text with ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift and other supplied implementation changes: peer signature/identity enforcement, socket ownership, lease expiry and lock fallback, cancellation/draining and model unloading, and recovery of inference admission. Check that busy-state reporting does not substitute for local rejection or alter live serving authorization (TB-011/T-053), and distinguish provider behavior from the separately owned coordinator contract. These units contain BASE documentation rather than implementation, and the patch ends within the new boundary; therefore this pass cannot validate the hold controls or the complete threat-model update. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a missing control.
